title: Coursoll's worm-fenced field on the north bank (1812)
items: A zigzag rail fence now closes a field on the north bank, west of the houses across the river from the fort, where Whistler's 1808 plan letters 'Mr Coursell' inside a 'Worm Fence'.
Quaife reads it as 'a house and inclosed field north of the river, belonging to Mr. Coursoll'. The house is the westernmost of the three houses the plan draws there, and is still to come.
Its place, size and rails follow the same rule as everything else the plan draws outside the fort, and are recorded as a liberty on its card.
